thread:
alex: quick q — for the /generate endpoint, should clients ever retry on 422 (validation) responses? saw a downstream service doing retries and it made me nervous

tamir: generally treat 422 as terminal — it's client-side validation. 429 + 5xx are retryable. that said there are fuzzy cases (transient validation conditions)

sophia: +1. we should be explicit in the contract. current guidance in api-contract.md says 4xx = client error, don't retry. 429 = rate limit, retry with backoff. 5xx = server transient.

alex: example we observed: a service returns 422 for "schema ingestion in progress" which is effectively transient. client retried and eventually succeeded. i get why they retried but now i'm worried about assumptions.

tamir: if it's truly transient it should either be 429/409 or include a Retry-After header. returning 422 without a signal is ambiguous.

sophia: options: a) change status to 429/409 for transient validation b) add a platform header (e.g. `X-RW-Retryable: 1`) c) include `retryable: true` in error JSON. adding fields is backwards-compatible, but SDKs need to honor them.

alex: lightweight preference: keep 422 = terminal by default, but runtime can opt into header `X-RW-Retryable` or JSON `error.retryable=true` for the few transient cases. SDKs should not retry plain 4xx.

maria: (fyi on PTO but catching up) that sounds reasonable. SDKs should implement: retry only on 5xx or 429 or when header/json indicates retryable. also respect `Retry-After` when present.

sophia: i'll update api-contract.md to spell this out and add an example. will also note streaming edge-cases.

tamir: i'll open a tiny RFC + runtime issue: runtime will set `X-RW-Retryable` on known transient validation errors (schema-locks, short maintenance windows). we should include tests.

alex: i'll take point on the SDK change if maria can't patch quickly. plan for: SDK guard + unit tests, docs update, runtime header implementation.

sophia: suggested client policy to document: "retry on 429/5xx or on explicit retryable signal (header or `error.retryable`) using exp backoff with max 3 attempts". i'll add the snippet.

alex: quick code example to use in the docs:
```
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
X-RW-Retryable: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "error": {
    "code": "temp-schema-lock",
    "message": "schema ingestion in progress",
    "retryable": true
  }
}
```

tamir: small note on streaming: if midstream validation fails, prefer a 5xx or stream-level error signal so clients can decide. midstream `422` semantics are messy.

maria: ack. i'll review the SDK patch later this week (back from PTO fri). if not, alex please go ahead.

alex: thanks. action items: sophia -> docs update, tamir -> runtime issue/RFC, alex/maria -> SDK guard. i'll create the issues and link here. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-check: all tests passed on branch `errsem/retryable-422` (CI #4821)

sophia: nice, thanks infra-bot. will link the PR in the RFC.

alex: resolving for now, will reopen if any client complains. :eyes:
